title: Chicken shawarma-style traybake with garlic {yoghurt}
blurb: Thighs, crisp potatoes and peppers roasted in warm allspice and cumin, with a lemony garlic {yoghurt} to spoon over.
steps: Heat the oven to {oven 220}. Tip the potatoes onto a large tray with half the oil and a pinch of salt and roast for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix the chicken with the crushed garlic, cumin, paprika, allspice, cinnamon, turmeric, the juice of half the lemon, the rest of the oil, the remaining salt and the black pepper.
Take the tray out, push the potatoes to one side and add the chicken, {red pepper} and onion. Roast for 20–25 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is cooked through and the edges are charred.
Stir the grated garlic into the {yoghurt} with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.
Pile the traybake onto plates, spoon over the garlic {yoghurt}, scatter with parsley and serve with the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

title: Kafta with buttery rice, lemon tahini and sumac onions
blurb: Herby, allspice-scented beef fingers over fluffy rice with a nutty tahini sauce and tangy pink onions.
steps: Squeeze the grated onion in your hands to remove the juice, then mix it with the {beef mince|ground beef}, half the parsley, the allspice, cinnamon, paprika, {qty 2|teaspoon|teaspoons} of salt and the black pepper. Shape into 8 short fingers.
Toss the sliced red onion with the sumac, the juice of half the lemon and a pinch of salt and leave to soften.
Rinse the rice, then cook it in plenty of boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes. Drain and let it steam dry for 2 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the kafta for 8–10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Whisk the tahini with the garlic, the rest of the lemon juice, a pinch of salt and {ml 50} cold water until pourable and pale.
Serve the kafta on the rice with the tomatoes and sumac onions, drizzle with the tahini and finish with the remaining parsley.

title: Mujadara with crispy onions and lemon tahini
blurb: Spiced Puy lentils and rice under a heap of deep-brown onions, with a crunchy tomato salad and tahini.
steps: Heat {ml 45} of the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, add the onions with a pinch of salt and cook for 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown and crisp at the edges. Lift half out onto a plate.
Meanwhile, put the lentils in a saucepan with the {stock cube}, cumin, allspice, cinnamon and {ml 600} water. Bring to the boil and simmer for 12 minutes.
Rinse the rice and stir it into the lentils with the remaining salt. Cover and cook on a low heat for 12–15 minutes until both are tender and the water is absorbed. Rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Toss the cucumber, tomatoes and parsley with the remaining oil, half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Whisk the tahini with the rest of the lemon juice, black pepper and {ml 40} cold water.
Stir the onions from the pan through the lentils and rice, top with the reserved crispy onions and serve with the salad and tahini.

title: Maghmour-style baked {aubergine} and chickpeas
blurb: Silky roast {aubergine} and chickpeas in a garlicky tomato sauce with a tang of pomegranate molasses.
steps: Heat the oven to {oven 220}. Toss the {aubergine} with {ml 30} of the oil and a teaspoon of salt on a large tray and roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until soft and golden.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a large ovenproof pan over a medium heat and soften the onion for 6–8 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, cinnamon and {chilli flakes} and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, pomegranate molasses, the remaining salt and the black pepper and simmer for 8 minutes until thickened.
Fold the roasted {aubergine} through the sauce and bake for 10 minutes. Warm the {pitta} in the oven for the last 2 minutes.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the warm {pitta} for scooping.

title: Shish taouk-style chicken skewers with garlic {yoghurt}
blurb: {Yoghurt}-marinated chicken with lemon, garlic and paprika, charred on skewers and tucked into warm {pitta}.
steps: Mix {g 100} of the {yoghurt} with two-thirds of the garlic, the {tomato puree}, paprika, allspice, the zest of the lemon, the oil, {qty 2|teaspoon|teaspoons} of salt and the black pepper. Stir in the chicken and leave for 10 minutes, or longer if you have time.
Heat the {grill|broiler} to high. Thread the chicken onto skewers, alternating with the {red pepper} and onion chunks.
{Grill|Broil} the skewers for 12–14 minutes, turning every few minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and charred in places.
Stir the rest of the garlic, a squeeze of lemon juice and a pinch of salt into the remaining {yoghurt}.
Warm the {pitta} under the {grill|broiler} for 30 seconds each side. Serve the skewers in the {pitta} with the cucumber, mint and garlic {yoghurt}, with the rest of the lemon cut into wedges.

title: Batata harra potatoes with fried eggs
blurb: Crisp fried potatoes tossed in garlic, {chilli}, lemon and fresh {coriander}, topped with runny eggs.
steps: Boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 7–8 minutes until just tender at the edges, then drain and let them steam dry for 3 minutes.
Heat {ml 30} of the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the potatoes for 12–15 minutes, turning only now and then, until crisp and golden all over.

Add the garlic, {chilli}, ground {coriander} and {chilli flakes} and fry for 1 minute, shaking the pan, until fragrant. Take off the heat and toss with half the {coriander}, the juice of half the lemon and the black pepper.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil in a second pan over a medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes until the whites are set and crisp at the edges.
Divide the potatoes between plates, top with the tomatoes and eggs, and finish with the rest of the {coriander} and a squeeze of lemon.

title: Lamb and rice stuffed {red peppers} with minted {yoghurt}
blurb: Sweet roast peppers filled with allspice-spiced lamb, rice and toasted pine nuts in a tomato bath.
steps: Heat the oven to {oven 200}. Boil the rice in salted water for 6 minutes, then drain.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, add the onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add the {lamb mince|ground lamb}, garlic, allspice and cinnamon and fry for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the {tomato puree}, the drained rice, the pine nuts, half the parsley, {qty 2|teaspoon|teaspoons} of salt and the black pepper.
Stand the pepper halves in a snug baking dish and spoon the filling into them. Mix the passata with {ml 100} water and a pinch of salt and pour it around the peppers.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10 minutes more until the peppers are soft and the tops are lightly browned.
Stir the mint into the {yoghurt} and serve with the peppers, spooning over some of the sauce and the rest of the parsley.

title: Fatteh-style chickpeas with garlic {yoghurt} and crisp {pitta}
blurb: Warm spiced chickpeas over crunchy {pitta}, drowned in tahini {yoghurt} and finished with sizzling pine nuts.
steps: Heat the oven to {oven 200}. Toss the {pitta} with {ml 10} of the oil and a pinch of salt on a tray and bake for 8 minutes until golden and crisp.
Whisk the {yoghurt} with the tahini, garlic, the juice of half the lemon and a good pinch of salt until smooth.

Heat {ml 10} of the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat, add the chickpeas, cumin, paprika and black pepper and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring, until hot and lightly crisped. Squeeze in a little lemon juice.
Wipe the pan, add the last of the oil and the pine nuts and toast for 1–2 minutes until golden.
Layer the {pitta} in bowls, spoon over the chickpeas, then the {yoghurt}, and finish with the pine nuts and their oil, the parsley and the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

title: Seven-spice chicken and bulgur pilaf with almonds
blurb: Chicken and nutty bulgur cooked together in a warm Lebanese-style spice blend, finished with toasted almonds.
steps: Mix the allspice, cinnamon, cumin, paprika, ground {coriander} and black pepper in a small bowl. This is your seven-spice-style blend.
Heat {ml 15} of the oil in a deep frying pan with a lid over a medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 5 minutes. Lift out onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the onion to the pan and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, the spice mix and the {tomato puree} and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the bulgur, crumble in the {stock cube} and add {ml 350} boiling water and the salt. Return the chicken, cover and simmer very gently for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes. Rest the pilaf off the heat for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and serve topped with the almonds and parsley, with the {yoghurt} on the side.

title: Lebanese-style lentil and spinach soup with lemon
blurb: A comforting red lentil soup with wilted spinach, cumin and a sharp squeeze of lemon.
steps: Heat {ml 20} of the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot with a pinch of salt for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and ground {coriander} and cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, crumble in the {stock cubes} and pour in {ml 900} boiling water. Simmer for 15–18 minutes until the lentils have broken down.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 2 minutes until wilted. Blend roughly with a stick blender if you like a smoother soup.
Season with the juice of the lemon, the remaining salt and the black pepper, and serve with the last of the oil and the {coriander} on top.

title: Samke harra-style fish with tahini and {chilli} {coriander}
blurb: Roast white fish with cumin, spooned with lemony tahini and a fiery garlic and {coriander} relish, over rice.
steps: Heat the oven to {oven 200}. Rub the fish with the cumin, half the oil, a teaspoon of salt and the black pepper, lay it on a lined tray and bake for 10–12 minutes until it flakes easily.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook it in plenty of boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Crush {qty 2|clove|cloves} of garlic with a pinch of salt and mix with the {chilli}, {coriander}, the juice of {qty 0.5|lemon|lemons} and the remaining oil to make a relish.
Whisk the tahini with the last clove of garlic, the juice of the other lemon half, a pinch of salt and {ml 50} cold water until smooth and pourable.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Serve the fish over the rice with the tahini sauce, the {chilli} relish and the pine nuts, with the second lemon cut into wedges.

title: Persian-style herb kuku with walnuts and {yoghurt}
blurb: A thick, bright-green herb frittata studded with walnuts, baked until set and served with cool {yoghurt}.
steps: Heat the oven to {oven 180}. Brush a {cm 20} ovenproof frying pan with half the oil.
Whisk the eggs with the turmeric, flour, baking powder, {qty 2|teaspoon|teaspoons} of salt and the black pepper until smooth.
Stir in the parsley, {coriander}, dill, {spring onions}, spinach and walnuts so the mixture is more herb than egg.
Heat the pan over a medium heat, pour in the mixture and cook for 3 minutes until the base starts to set, then transfer to the oven for 20–25 minutes until firm in the centre and golden.
Warm the {pitta} in the oven for the last 2 minutes. Season the {yoghurt} with a pinch of salt and the remaining oil.
Turn the kuku out, cut into wedges and serve with the {yoghurt}, cucumber and warm {pitta}.

title: Iraqi-style tomato and white bean stew with rice
blurb: Soft cannellini beans simmered in a baharat-scented tomato sauce with lemon, spooned over fluffy rice.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat and cook the onion with a pinch of salt for 7–8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, {tomato puree}, cumin, cinnamon, allspice and paprika and cook, stirring, for 1–2 minutes.

Stir in the tomatoes, the beans, {ml 150} water, {qty 2|teaspoon|teaspoons} of salt and the black pepper. Simmer for 15–18 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and the beans are creamy.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook it in plenty of boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, then drain.
Finish the stew with the juice of half the lemon, spoon it over the rice and scatter with parsley, with the rest of the lemon cut into wedges.

title: Turkish-style lamb pide with peppers and egg
blurb: Boat-shaped {yoghurt} flatbreads piled with spiced lamb and peppers, baked hot with a runny egg in the middle.
steps: Heat the oven to {oven 240} with a large tray inside. Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the {lamb mince|ground lamb} for 5 minutes until browned.
Add the onion, {red pepper}, garlic, {tomato puree}, paprika, cumin, {chilli flakes}, a teaspoon of salt and the black pepper and cook for 6–8 minutes until dry and fragrant. Cool for a few minutes.

Mix the flour, baking powder and {qty 2|teaspoon|teaspoons} of salt with {g 180} of the {yoghurt} to a soft dough, then knead briefly on a floured surface. Divide into {qty 2} equal pieces and roll each piece into a long oval about {cm 30} long.
Pinch the long edges up and in to make a boat shape with a rim, then spoon the lamb mixture into the middle, leaving the rim clear.
Slide the pides onto the hot tray and bake for 10 minutes. Make a well in each filling, crack in an egg, and bake for 3–4 minutes more until the egg is just set.
Scatter with parsley, squeeze over some lemon and serve with the remaining {yoghurt} on the side.

title: Syrian-style lentil kibbeh bowls with pomegranate
blurb: Spiced red lentil and bulgur patties, crisp outside and tender within, in a fresh salad bowl with tahini.
steps: Simmer the lentils in {ml 300} water with a pinch of salt for 10–12 minutes until soft and the water has been absorbed. Stir in the bulgur, cover and leave off the heat for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat {ml 20} of the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and cook the onions for 8–10 minutes until golden. Stir in the allspice, cinnamon, cumin, paprika and {tomato puree} and cook for 1 minute.
Mix the onions into the lentil mixture with the flour, walnuts, {qty 2|teaspoon|teaspoons} of salt and the black pepper. Let it cool for 5 minutes, then shape into 8 small patties with damp hands.
Wipe out the pan, heat {ml 25} of the oil over a medium-high heat and fry the patties for 3–4 minutes on each side until crisp and golden.
Whisk the tahini with half the lemon juice, a pinch of salt and {ml 40} cold water. Toss the cucumber, tomato, leaves and parsley with the pomegranate molasses and the rest of the lemon juice.
Divide the salad between bowls, top with the patties and drizzle with the tahini.

title: Chicken, lemon and olive tagine with couscous
blurb: Tender chicken simmered with ginger, turmeric, soft lemon and green olives, piled over herby couscous.
steps: Season the chicken with a teaspoon of salt and the black pepper. Heat {ml 15} of the oil in a wide casserole or deep pan over a medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 5 minutes. Lift out onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the onion and cook for 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric and cinnamon and cook for 1 minute.
Cut {qty 1|lemon|lemons} into thin slices, discarding the pips. Return the chicken to the pan with the lemon slices, the olives, the {stock cube} and {ml 300} boiling water.
Cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes, then uncover and cook for 5 minutes more to thicken the sauce.
Put the couscous in a bowl with a pinch of salt and the juice of the second lemon, pour over {ml 200} boiling water, cover for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
Stir half the {coriander} through the couscous, spoon the tagine over and scatter with the rest.

title: Moroccan harira-style soup with chickpeas and lentils
blurb: A warming tomato soup with lentils, chickpeas, cinnamon and ginger, finished with lemon and a lot of fresh herbs.
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat and cook the onion, celery and carrot with a pinch of salt for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in the garlic, {tomato puree}, turmeric, ginger, cinnamon and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, lentils, chickpeas, {stock cubes} and {ml 800} boiling water. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the orzo and simmer for 8–10 minutes until tender, adding a splash of water if the soup gets too thick.
Add half the {coriander} and parsley, the juice of half the lemon, the remaining salt and the black pepper, and serve topped with the rest of the herbs and the remaining lemon cut into wedges.
